name: nm49
question: Does nm25 re-trained with the partner's aggressive and odd-sized players (2 extreme bluffers, 2 all-in players, 2 raising 3x, 2 raising 5x, 1 raising 8x) added to its usual rule players win more than nm25 against those players without losing to anyone else?
why: The partner, after playing Kestrel on 2026-11-27, proposed training against this pool. The players are new rule players (ninemax_selfplay: bluffer, jammer, raise3x, raise5x, raise8x; the raisers on their own bet menus, so the network meets those sizes). nm25 already beats each by a lot (4,000 deals x 9: +321 bb/100 against 8 bluffers, +531 against 8 all-in players, +26, +34 and +41 against the raisers), and nm46, trained against an aggressive pool, beat nm25 against the bluffers by +5.5 [+1.8, +9.3]; so the run can only add to large wins, and the risk is what nm45 showed: training on a narrow pool can cost the win against players it no longer sees (the calling station, -16.5). The new players are added to nm25's usual pool (reg, reg, tag, maniac, station), not in place of it (decided 2026-11-27), so the players nm25 trained against stay in training; the checks hold it to nm25's level against them too.

checks.why: it must not lose to nm25 in nm25's own game

the point of the run: on the same deals as nm25, the 95% interval of the difference must lie above zero against each of the pool's kinds (raise3x left out: its size is nm25's own open, nothing new to learn)
nm45's check: with nine new players the old ones come up less often in training (5 of 14 pool entries), so the station's win must not fall (interval above -2.0 against each)
at least as good as nm25 on average across 25 generated players, and never far behind
bluff jams and raises must lose prize equity against it, as against nm25
as nm45 and nm47: the mean of four 30-minute exploiters, limit nm25's +0.75 plus 0.5; a network bent towards calling aggressive players is easier to exploit
